# Allele Frequencies & HWE

This chapter covers estimating allele and genotype frequencies, testing for Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium, and rarefaction analysis.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(gstudio)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
data(arapat)
```
:::


## Allele Frequencies

The `frequencies()` function is an S3 generic that works on both individual locus vectors and entire data.frames.

### Single Locus


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
arapat |>
  pull(LTRS) |>
  frequencies()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
  Allele Frequency
1     01  0.523416
2     02  0.476584
```


:::
:::


### Entire Data Frame

When applied to a data.frame, `frequencies()` returns frequencies for all locus columns:

```{.r .cell-code}
  filter(Locus %in% c("LTRS", "WNT"))
```

## Genotype Counts and Frequencies

### Genotype Counts per Stratum

The `genotype_counts()` function summarizes non-missing genotype counts per locus, optionally by stratum:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
arapat |>
  genotype_counts()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
    Stratum   N LTRS WNT  EN  EF ZMP AML ATPS MP20
ALL     ALL 363  363 352 360 361 330 340  363  358
```


:::
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
arapat |>
  genotype_counts(stratum = "Species")
```


### Genotype Frequencies

The `genotype_frequencies()` function returns observed and expected genotype counts for a locus vector:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
arapat |>
  pull(LTRS) |>
  genotype_frequencies()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

1    01:01      147  99.44904
2    01:02       86 181.10193
3    02:02      130  82.44904
```

## Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium

The `hwe.test()` function tests for HWE using a chi-square approximation.  A single locus gives a standard test, printed like `chisq.test()`:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
arapat |>
  filter(Species == "Mainland") |>
  pull(LTRS) |>
  hwe.test()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr}

```
Warning in .hwe_chisq(x[[loci]], label = loci, suppress_warnings =
suppress_warnings): Under 50 samples for pull(filter(arapat, Species ==
"Mainland"), LTRS) this may not be a good approximation.
```


:::

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr}

```
Warning in .hwe_chisq(x[[loci]], label = loci, suppress_warnings =
suppress_warnings): Fewer than 5 genotypes expected at pull(filter(arapat,
Species == "Mainland"), LTRS) consider collapsing alleles.
```


:::

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

	Chi-square test for Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium with continuity
	correction

data:  pull(filter(arapat, Species == "Mainland"), LTRS)
X-squared = 0.90828, df = 1, p-value = 0.3406
```


:::
:::


Several loci, or a `stratum`, give a table with one row per test: the chi-square statistic, degrees of freedom, p-value and method.  Significant p-values indicate departures from HWE expectations.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
arapat |>
  hwe.test(stratum = "Species", loci = c("LTRS", "WNT"))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
    Stratum Locus  statistic df      p.value
1      Cape  LTRS  2.7682735  1 9.614982e-02
2      Cape   WNT 38.1273682  1 6.627400e-10
3  Mainland  LTRS  0.9082806  1 3.405710e-01
4  Mainland   WNT 29.2542373  1 6.347726e-08
5 Peninsula  LTRS 46.9566665  1 7.257371e-12
6 Peninsula   WNT 85.1611263  6 3.056896e-16
                                                                     method
1 Chi-square test for Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium with continuity correction
2 Chi-square test for Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium with continuity correction
3 Chi-square test for Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium with continuity correction
4 Chi-square test for Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium with continuity correction
5                            Chi-square test for Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium
6 Chi-square test for Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium with continuity correction
```

### Interpreting Results

Departures from HWE can arise from:

- Non-random mating (inbreeding, assortative mating)
- Population substructure (Wahlund effect)
- Selection at or near the marker locus
- Small population size (genetic drift)

## Rarefaction

Diversity statistics such as allelic richness grow with sample size, so strata sampled unequally cannot be compared directly.  `rarefaction.test()` rarefies each locus to the smallest number of genotyped individuals in any stratum: every larger stratum is resampled `nperm` times without replacement at that size, and the table gives the observed value, the mean across resamples (`estimate`) and a percentile interval (`conf.low`, `conf.high`) for each stratum, locus and mode.  With several loci, a `Multilocus` row per stratum combines each resample across loci.  It is `NA` for a stratum missing any of the loci, so strata are compared over the same loci; `na.rm = TRUE` combines the loci that are available instead.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
set.seed(1)
rare <- arapat |>
  rarefaction.test(stratum = "Species", mode = c("A", "Ae"), nperm = 199)
rare |>
  filter(Locus == "Multilocus")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

	Rarefaction without replacement (199 resamples)

data:  arapat by Species
size:  smallest stratum at each locus
95 percent percentile interval of the resampled values

    Stratum      Locus Mode  N size observed estimate conf.low conf.high
1      Cape Multilocus    A NA   NA    2.625    2.318    2.125     2.625
2      Cape Multilocus   Ae NA   NA    1.391    1.387    1.310     1.460
3  Mainland Multilocus    A NA   NA    3.625    3.625    3.625     3.625
4  Mainland Multilocus   Ae NA   NA    1.979    1.979    1.979     1.979
5 Peninsula Multilocus    A NA   NA    4.875    3.519    3.119     3.881
6 Peninsula Multilocus   Ae NA   NA    2.208    2.156    2.012     2.330
```


:::
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
rare |>
  filter(Mode == "A", Locus != "Multilocus") |>
  ggplot(aes(Locus, estimate, colour = Stratum)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high),
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  labs(y = "Rarefied allelic richness") +
  theme_minimal()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](allele-frequencies_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-14-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::


Set `size =` to rarefy to a fixed number of individuals instead; strata with fewer genotypes at a locus are `NA`.  The resampled values for each row are kept in the list-column `values`, which printing hides.

## Optimal Sampling

The `optimal_sampling()` function estimates how many individuals are needed to capture a given proportion of allelic diversity:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
arapat |>
  pull(LTRS) |>
  optimal_sampling(nrep = 99)
```
:::


## Without Pipes


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
frequencies(arapat$LTRS)
frequencies(arapat, stratum = "Species")
frequencies(arapat, loci = c("LTRS", "WNT"))
frequency_matrix(arapat, stratum = "Species")
genotype_counts(arapat, stratum = "Species")
genotype_frequencies(arapat$LTRS)
hwe.test(arapat[arapat$Species == "Mainland", ])
rare <- rarefaction.test(arapat, stratum = "Species", mode = c("A", "Ae"), nperm = 199)
rare[rare$Locus == "Multilocus", ]
optimal_sampling(arapat$LTRS, nrep = 99)
```
:::
